raw_segments.text: Kneeling by the body, O child, my daughter's child, Who held as true my castle walls,
And to the folk a name of fear thou wast, And no man sought to shame my grey beard
When they knew that thou wast there, Else had they swift reward.
And now I fare forth in dishonor outcast I the great Cadmus,
Who sowed the seed rows of this state of Thebes, And reaped the harvest wonderful.
O my beloved, though thy heart is dull in death, O still beloved and always beloved.
Never more, then, shalt thou lay thine hand To this white beard, and speak to me thy mother's father.
Ask who wrongeth thee? Who stints thine honor, Or with malice stirs thine heart?
Speak, and I smite thine injurers.
But now, O, woe to me and thee also, Woe to thy mother and her sisters, woe all way.
O, whoso walketh not in dread of gods, Let him but look on this man dead.
